'''Claire Marie Valdez''' (born October 12, 1989)<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.qchron.com/qboro/i_have_often_walked/claire-valdez-traveled-from-texas-to-ridgewood/article_ccd35d9d-d58c-55a9-9fd6-c731b0716344.html |title=Claire Valdez traveled from Texas to Ridgewood |last=Marzlock |first=Ron |work=[[Queens Chronicle]] |date=July 2, 2026 |access-date=July 2, 2026}}</ref> is an American politician who is the [[U.S. Representative|U.S. Representative-elect]] for [[New York's 7th congressional district]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/new-york-us-house-district-7-results |title=New York House District 7 General Election Results 2026 |website=[[NBC News]] |access-date=November 4, 2026}}</ref> A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and the [[Democratic Socialists of America]], has served as a member of the [[New York State Assembly]] for the [[New York's 37th State Assembly district|37th district]] since 2025, representing part of the Borough of [[Queens]].

==Early life and education==
Originally from [[Lubbock, Texas|Lubbock]], [[Texas]], Valdez moved to [[New York City]] in 2015 and lives in [[Ridgewood, Queens]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/personality/2025/01/meet-2025-class-new-state-lawmakers/402275/?oref=csny-skybox-hp|title=Meet the 2025 class of new state lawmakers|last=Jefferson|first=Austin|website=[[City & State]]|date=January 17, 2025|access-date=January 21, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hogan |first=Bernadette |date=2024-06-21 |title=Queens voters head to polls in Assembly District 37 Democratic primary |url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2024/06/21/queens-voters-head-to-polls-in-assembly-district-37 |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=ny1.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="QNS-2023-08-30">{{Cite web |last=Parry |first=Bill |date=2023-08-30 |title=Ridgewood woman launches campaign to unseat scandal-scarred Assemblyman Juan Ardila |url=https://qns.com/2023/08/ridgewood-woman-campaign-unseat-ardila/ |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=qns.com |language=en-US}}</ref> She is a member of the [[Democratic Socialists of America]] and Socialist Majority Caucus.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=López⁩ |first1=Álvaro |last2=Turner |first2=David |date=October 16, 2024 |title=For A Fighting & Winning NYC-DSA |url=https://www.socialistmajority.com/theagitator/winning-nyc-dsa |access-date=October 26, 2025 |work=The Agitator}}</ref> She is "a [[Multiple citizenship|dual citizen]] of [[Ysleta del Sur Pueblo]] Nation and the United States."<ref name="Ja2026" />

Valdez received her [[Bachelor of Fine Arts]] from the [[School of the Art Institute of Chicago]], studying painting and art history.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bishara |first=Hakim |date=2026-06-16 |url=https://hyperallergic.com/claire-valdez-wants-to-be-your-artist-in-congress/ |title=Claire Valdez Wants to Be Your Artist in Congress |website=Hyperallergic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://thevisualist.org/2014/12/pineapple-ribbon-new-works-by-erol-scott-harris-claire-valdez/ |title=Erol Scott Harris & Claire Valdez: Pineapple Ribbon |website=The Visualist}}</ref> She worked a series of service jobs, including at [[Taco Bell]], [[Pizza Hut]], and [[Trader Joe's]], before moving to New York City to pursue a career in art.<ref name="Ja2026" />

==Early career==
After graduating from college, Valdez worked as a program assistant in the visual arts department at [[Columbia University]] before beginning her term as an assembly member.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Freeman |first=Harper |date=2024-07-24 |title=A worker first, unionist second, Valdez seeks Queens Assembly seat |url=https://thechiefleader.com/stories/a-worker-first-unionist-second-valdez-seeks-queens-assembly-seat,52788 |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=The Chief |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Ja2026">{{cite web |last1=Uetricht |first1=Micah |last2=Valdez |first2=Claire |title=Claire Valdez Is a Socialist and Union Organizer Running for Congress |url=https://jacobin.com/2026/01/claire-valdez-union-organizing-congress |website=[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin.com]] |access-date=8 January 2026 |language=en-US |date=8 January 2026}}</ref> While working at Columbia, she became an active member of [[United Auto Workers]] Local 2110 and was elected unit chair in the local.<ref name="QNS-2023-08-30" />

In 2019, Valdez joined the [[New York City Democratic Socialists of America|New York City chapter]] of the [[Democratic Socialists of America]] and went on to serve as the New Member Coordinator.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farghaly |first=Mohamed |date=2026-03-19 |title=Claire Valdez Brings Labor Fight to Congressional Race |url=https://queensledger.com/2026/03/19/claire-valdez-brings-labor-fight-to-congressional-race/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Queens Ledger |language=en-US}}</ref> She has worked on many of the chapter's electoral projects, including [[Julia Salazar]]'s 2020 reelection and Samy Olivares's 2022 campaign for New York State Assembly.<ref name="Ja2026" />

== New York State Assembly ==
In the [[2024 New York State Assembly election]], Valdez was a candidate in the [[New York's 37th State Assembly district|37th district]]. The incumbent, [[Juan Ardila]], was seen as vulnerable to a primary challenge after two women accused him of [[sexual assault]] and misconduct.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Rebecca C. |date=2023-05-08 |title=Queens progressives look to primary Juan Ardila if he refuses to resign |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2023/05/queens-progressives-look-primary-juan-ardila-if-he-refuses-resign/386061/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> In the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] primary, Valdez defeated Ardila by 48 percentage points and moderate Johanna Carmona by 27 percentage points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krichevsky |first=Sophie |date=2024-06-27 |title=Valdez wins AD 37 race by 27 points |url=https://www.qchron.com/editions/queenswide/valdez-wins-ad-37-race-by-27-points/article_ec63682e-5a2c-509a-b104-579aae68d09b.html |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=Queens Chronicle |language=en}}</ref> She was endorsed by Congresswoman [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], [[Democratic Socialists of America]], and the [[Working Families Party]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parry |first=Bill |date=2023-11-16 |title=Working Families Party endorses Claire Valdez in race to unseat Assemblymember Juan Ardila |url=https://queenspost.com/working-families-party-endorses-claire-valdez-in-race-to-unseat-assemblymember-juan-ardila |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=Queens Post |language=en-US |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240801234708/https://queenspost.com/working-families-party-endorses-claire-valdez-in-race-to-unseat-assemblymember-juan-ardila |archive-date=2024-08-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Andres |first=Czarinna |date=2024-05-23 |title=AOC endorses fellow Democratic Socialist Claire Valdez for New York Assembly District 37 |url=https://queenspost.com/aoc-endorses-fellow-democratic-socialist-claire-valdez-for-new-york-assembly-district-37 |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=Queens Post |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwach |first=Ryan |date=2024-06-11 |title=Ardila challengers split incumbent's former supporters as election nears |url=https://queenseagle.com/all/2024/6/11/ardila-challengers-split-incumbents-former-supporters-as-election-nears |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Queens Daily Eagle |language=en-US}}</ref> She ran unopposed in the November general election.

After launching her assembly campaign in 2023, Valdez called for a ceasefire in Gaza.<ref name=":4" /> Upon her election, she joined [[New York State Socialists in Office]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=2026-01-26 |title=What's a Socialist in Office? |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/01/whats-socialist-office/410941/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> She was arrested during a 2025 demonstration outside the offices of U.S. senators [[Chuck Schumer]] and [[Kirsten Gillibrand]], protesting their votes against a resolution halting U.S. sales of arms to Israel.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stack |first=Liam |last2=Schweber |first2=Nate |date=2025-08-01 |title=Gaza War Protesters Arrested at Offices of Schumer and Gillibrand |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/01/nyregion/gaza-war-protesters-schumer-gillibrand.html |access-date=2026-06-16 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> She has sponsored the Not On Our Dime Act, first introduced by [[Zohran Mamdani]] during his term in the assembly.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=2026-03-24 |title=Pro-Palestinian PAL PAC endorses Claire Valdez for Congress |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/03/pro-palestinian-pal-pac-endorses-claire-valdez-congress/412325/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> The pro-Israel Solidarity PAC spent over $40,000 to oppose her 2024 candidacy for New York State Assembly.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Gelardi |first1=Chris |last2=Rock |first2=Julia |date=2024-06-06 |title=Pro-Israel PAC Floods Assembly Races With Cash |url=https://nysfocus.com/2024/06/06/new-york-elections-israel-donations |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=New York Focus |language=en}}</ref>

Valdez is a sponsor of New York For All, which bars the use of state and local resources in federal immigration enforcement actions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bill Search and Legislative Information {{!}} New York State Assembly |url=https://nyassembly.gov/leg/?bn=A03506 |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=nyassembly.gov}}</ref> On September 28, 2025, she was arrested while inspecting the facilities at 26 Federal Plaza in Manhattan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=2025-09-18 |title=State and city lawmakers arrested at 26 Federal Plaza |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2025/09/state-and-city-lawmakers-arrested-26-federal-plaza/408218/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref>

Amid the [[Investigations into the Eric Adams administration|investigations]] into [[Mayor of New York City]] [[Eric Adams]], Valdez publicly called for his resignation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=2025-02-14 |title=With Eric Adams refusing to resign, who is calling for him to be removed from office? |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2025/02/eric-adams-refusing-resign-who-calling-him-be-removed-office/403032/ |access-date=2025-02-22 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> She endorsed [[Zohran Mamdani]] in the [[2025 New York City mayoral election]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=2025-03-13 |title=Zohran Mamdani endorsed by (most) socialist lawmakers |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2025/03/zohran-mamdani-endorsed-most-socialist-lawmakers/403716/ |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> She was among the early supporters of his campaign and the only elected official present at his October 2024 campaign launch.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwach |first=Ryan |date=2024-10-24 |title=Queens socialist pol announces bid for mayor |url=https://queenseagle.com/all/2024/10/24/queens-socialist-pol-announces-bid-for-mayor |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Queens Daily Eagle |language=en-US}}</ref>

On January 8, 2026, Valdez announced her candidacy for [[New York's 7th congressional district]] to succeed retiring incumbent [[Nydia Velázquez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/01/claire-valdez-launches-bid-congress-staffed-mamdanis-consigliere/410534/|title=Claire Valdez launches a bid for Congress staffed by Mamdani's consigliere|last1=Pretsky|last2=Sterne|first1=Holly|first2=Peter|date=January 8, 2026|access-date=January 8, 2026|website=[[City & State]]}}</ref> In the primary, she faced [[Brooklyn]] [[borough president]] [[Antonio Reynoso]] and [[New York City Council]]or [[Julie Won]].<ref name=":0" /> The race was seen as a fight between [[Progressivism|progressives]], who largely backed Reynoso, and [[Socialism|socialists]], who backed Valdez.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wimbish |first=Whitney Curry |date=2026-06-17 |title=In New York's 'Commie Corridor,' a Race Over How to Build Power |url=https://prospect.org/2026/06/17/new-york-commie-corridor-valdez-reynoso-seventh-district-congressional-race/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=The American Prospect |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fandos |first=Nicholas |date=2026-06-01 |title=The Congressional Primary Tearing the Mamdani Coalition in Two |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/01/nyregion/nyc-primary-antonio-reynoso-claire-valdez-mamdani.html |access-date=2026-06-24 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Tarleton |first=John |date=June 11, 2026 |title=NY 2026 Democratic Primaries: Left vs. Establishment Divide Deepens |url=https://indypendent.org/2026/06/left-vs-establishment-divide-deepens/ |website=The Indypendent |access-date=2026-06-24 |language=en-US}}</ref> Valdez was endorsed by New York City mayor [[Zohran Mamdani]], Senator [[Bernie Sanders]], [[New York City Democratic Socialists of America|NYC-DSA]], [[Justice Democrats]], and the [[United Auto Workers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Claire Valdez |url=https://justicedemocrats.com/candidate/claire-valdez/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Justice Democrats |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Endorsements {{!}} Bernie Sanders Official Website |url=https://bsanders-astro.pages.dev/endorse/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=bsanders-astro.pages.dev |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= O'Brien |first= Shane |date= 2026-01-09 |title= Mamdani, UAW endorse AM Claire Valdez for NY-7 Congressional seat |url= https://qns.com/2026/01/mamdani-uaw-endorse-am-claire-valdez-for-ny-7-congressional-seat/ |access-date= 2026-06-16 |website= qns.com |language= en-US}}</ref> Reynoso received the support of Velázquez and the [[Working Families Party]] and received the majority of labor union endorsements.<ref name=":2" />

Valdez, along with fellow Mamdani-endorsed congressional candidates [[Brad Lander]] and [[Darializa Avila Chevalier]], received outside support from the pro-Palestine super PAC [[American Priorities]], which was created to counter the influence of [[AIPAC]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Goldenberg |first=Sally |date=June 23, 2026 |title=$50 Million Spent on N.Y. Primaries Includes A.I. and AIPAC Money |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/23/nyregion/new-york-primary-campaign-spending.html |access-date=June 24, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> AIPAC did not directly involve itself in the campaign.<ref name=":1" />

On May 14, Valdez's campaign ratified a union contract under the [[Campaign Workers Guild]], becoming the first campaign in New York to unionize during the 2026 election cycle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sterne |first=Peter |date=2026-05-15 |title=Claire Valdez campaign staff unionizes – the first in NY this year |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/05/claire-valdez-campaign-staff-unionizes-first-ny-year/413595/ |access-date=2026-06-26 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref>

On June 23, Valdez defeated Reynoso and Won.<!--Not a typo. Won was one of her opponents.--><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Deanna |date=2026-06-23 |title=Claire Valdez wins NY-7 Democratic primary, Spectrum News says |url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2026/06/24/nyc-june-2026-primary-7th-congressional-district-democratic-winner |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=ny1.com |language=en}}</ref> She was expected to win the general election, as New York's 7th district was considered a [[safe seat]] with a [[Cook Partisan Voting Index]] of D+25.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-03 |title=2025 Cook PVI℠: District Map and List (119th Congress) |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/cook-pvi/2025-partisan-voting-index/district-map-and-list |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Cook Political Report |language=en}}</ref> She did win, making her the first Native American woman to represent New York in Congress.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ictnews.org/politics/election-2026/seven-native-candidates-battle-for-the-u-s-house/|title=8 Native candidates battle for the U.S. House|first=Jourdan|last=Bennett-Begaye|date=November 4, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://19thnews.org/2026/11/election-results-new-mexico-governor/|title=In Minnesota and New Mexico, midterms usher in historic representation for Native women|first=Jessica Kutz, Mel Leonor|last=Barclay|date=November 4, 2026}}</ref>

==Political positions==
{{Democratic Socialism US|politicians}}
=== Environment ===
As a State Assembly member, Valdez was the primary sponsor of legislation to create a state office to coordinate environmental sustainability policies at the [[State University of New York]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York A06348 {{!}} 2025-2026 {{!}} General Assembly |url=https://legiscan.com/NY/bill/A06348/2025 |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=LegiScan |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2026, Valdez and then-Assembly candidate [[Diana Moreno]] wrote an [[op-ed]] calling for a $200 million commitment to public renewable energy in the 2026 state budget.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Moreno |first1=Diana |last2=Valdez |first2=Claire |date=2026-01-10 |title= Hochul must embrace public power to ease energy costs |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2026/01/10/hochul-must-embrace-public-power-to-ease-energy-costs/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=New York Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Foreign policy ===

==== Iran ====
Valdez strongly opposes the [[2026 Iran war]]. In March 2026 she said that US intervention would cause "mass chaos and destruction"<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |last=Anuta |first=Joe |last2=Sommerfeldt |first2=Chris |date=March 3, 2026 |title=Iran war provides another litmus test for New York Democrats |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/03/iran-war-litmus-test-new-york-democrats-00807920 |access-date=July 31, 2026 |work=Politico}}</ref> and criticized congressional Democratic leaders for their rhetorical choices about the war, saying: "The emphasis on procedure and expecting the Trump administration to provide some evidence or rationale that supports this war is an abdication of our responsibility to say that we don't want another endless war".<ref name=":7" /> She also said, "The Iranian regime, the crushing of dissent in their own country, is of course awful, but military intervention from the U.S. is not going to solve that problem."<ref name=":7" />

==== Israel and Palestine ====
During her State Assembly campaign, Valdez advocated for a [[ceasefire]] in Gaza and was a vocal supporter of justice in Palestine.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lucas |first=Peter |date=2023-12-09 |title=This Union Organizer Is Hoping to Expand Socialists' Electoral Stronghold in Queens |url=https://jacobin.com/2023/12/claire-valdez-dsa-queens-new-york-state-assembly-juan-ardila-uaw |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=jacobin.com |language=en-US}}</ref> As an Assembly member, she sponsored the Not On Our Dime Act, which would prohibit New York nonprofits from supporting [[Israeli settlement]] activity.<ref name=":4" /> During her Congressional campaign, Valdez was a strong critic of Israel, calling its actions in Gaza a [[genocide]] and [[apartheid]] and supporting the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] if he came to New York.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Way |first=Katie |date=2026-06-09 |title=Assemblymember Claire Valdez is Running on 'Moral Clarity' on Israel and Gaza: 'So Many Democrats Stayed on the Sidelines and Said Nothing' |url=https://hellgatenyc.com/claire-valdez-running-on-moral-clarity-ny-7/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Hell Gate |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Brien |first=Shane |date=2026-06-04 |title=NY-7 candidates take part in first televised debate ahead of June 23 primary |url=https://qns.com/2026/06/ny-7-debate-june-primary/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=qns.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Stack |first=Liam |date=2026-06-24 |title=NY Jewish Leaders Wrestle With Israel Critics' Sweep in Primary Elections |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/24/nyregion/jewish-leaders-primary-reaction.html |access-date=2026-06-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

=== Housing ===
Valdez has advocated policies including universal [[Rent control in the United States|rent control]], construction of [[Public housing|social housing]], and stronger tenant protections. To enact rent control, she has supported helping states build county-level rent boards to set rents.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Chang |first=Clio |date=2026-06-24 |title=Why Claire Valdez Wants Universal Rent Control |url=https://www.curbed.com/article/claire-valdez-housing-plan-congress-exclusive-interview.html |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Curbed |language=en}}</ref>

In the State Assembly, Valdez co-sponsored a bill to build and finance the construction of new social housing.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jefferson |first=Austin C. |date=2024-02-06 |title=Lawmakers propose creation of state authority to finance and build affordable housing |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/policy/2024/02/lawmakers-propose-creation-state-authority-finance-and-build-affordable-housing/393946/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=City & State NY |language=en}}</ref> She supports the Homes Act, which would establish a federally backed development authority to build affordable public housing capped at 25% of a household's [[adjusted gross income]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-19 |title=U.S. Senator Tina Smith and Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez Introduce Homes Act to Tackle America's Housing Crisis {{!}} Representative Ocasio-Cortez |url=http://ocasio-cortez.house.gov/media/press-releases/us-senator-tina-smith-and-congresswoman-ocasio-cortez-introduce-homes-act |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=ocasio-cortez.house.gov |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

=== Labor ===
Valdez has advocated for significant labor law reform, including ending [[at-will employment]], a [[federal job guarantee]], and a [[four-day workweek]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=French |first=Nick |date=2026-04-22 |title=Claire Valdez's Bold Program for Labor in Congress |url=https://jacobin.com/2026/04/valdez-labor-left-congress-campaign |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=jacobin.com |language=en-US}}</ref> She has also expressed strong supports for unions, saying, "We're going to prioritize rebuilding the labor movement and getting every single worker into a union. And that's going to be priority number one for me when I'm in office."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Deanna |date=2026-06-25 |title=What are Claire Valdez's priorities for Congress? |url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/inside-city-hall/2026/06/25/what-are-claire-valdez-s-priorities-for-congress- |access-date=2026-06-26 |website=ny1.com |language=en}}</ref>

Valdez supports the [[Protecting the Right to Organize Act]], which would expand [[Labor rights|employees' rights]] to organize and [[Collective bargaining|collectively bargain]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=O'Brien |first=Shane |date=2026-01-28 |title=Claire Valdez puts union advocacy front and center in bid to succeed Velázquez in NY-7 |url=https://qns.com/2026/01/valdez-union-advocacy-ny-7/ |access-date=2026-06-26 |website=qns.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Healthcare ===
Valdez supports Medicare for All and transitioning to a [[single-payer healthcare]] system.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valdez |first=Claire |date=2026-05-31 |title=Why I'm running for Congress this year |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2026/05/31/claire-valdez-why-im-running-for-congress-this-year/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=New York Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Nationalizing US airlines ===
Valdez supports abolishing [[TSA PreCheck]] and nationalizing US airlines. On the "Bitchuation Room" podcast, she said the "airline industry is making a lot of money, and constantly undermining consumer rights, nickel-and-diming us in every single facet of having to fly someplace. And in a country where there's no robust national rail system, all we have are—it's planes or nothing if you want to get from one side of the country to the other. And so we're forced into these, like, super uncomfortable seats, we have very few rights, airline industry overbook flights. There are all kinds of ways that they're making the maximum profit at our discomfort, inconvenience, and great expense."<ref>{{Cite AV media |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iAF6ulPwSyc |title= Candidate Corner: Claire Valdez |date= 2026-05-01 |last= The Bitchuation Room (with Francesca Fiorentini) |access-date= 2026-06-28 |via= YouTube}}</ref>

=== Social issues ===
==== Immigration ====
Valdez has called for [[Abolish ICE|abolishing]] the [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) agency, naming it as one of her day-one legislative priorities in Congress.<ref name=":6" />
[[File:2026-09-22 Claire Valdez and Harvey Epstein at NYU-Langone-Rally Jack-Walker-Jatwa.jpg|alt=A woman and a man stand side by side holding up a white banner, looking onward. They are surrounded by pro-trans rights signs.|thumb|Valdez attends a 2026 protest against NYU Langone's decision to bar minors from gender-affirming care.]]

==== LGBTQ rights ====
Valdez is a proponent of [[LGBTQ rights in the United States|LGBTQ rights]]. She supports [[Transgender rights in the United States|transgender rights]], including funding for [[Transgender health care|gender-affirming care]] and the adoption of a Transgender Bill of Rights to provide anti-discrimination protection based on [[gender identity]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o6kfUzzOICk |title=Will Claire Valdez be the most Progressive in Congress |date=2026-05-15 |last=Mike From PA |access-date=2026-06-24 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Swenson |first=Jacob |date=2026-02-11 |title=Jayapal, Markey Introduce Landmark Trans Bill of Rights |url=https://admin-jayapal.house.gov/2026/02/11/jayapal-markey-introduce-landmark-trans-bill-of-rights-2/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal |language=en-US}}</ref>
